title: Sylvester Stallone
wiki_lead:
Sylvester Gardenzio Stallone (born July 6, 1946) is an American actor and filmmaker. He rose to fame as an action star for his memorable portrayals of boxer Rocky Balboa in the Rocky franchise (1976–present) and of soldier John Rambo in the Rambo franchise (1982–2019). Stallone usually portrayed underdog characters who conquer seemingly impossible challenges through perseverance and determination in his films, and his physically expressive and emotionally charged style of acting redefined the action hero.
Stallone took early roles in The Lords of Flatbush (1974) and Death Race 2000 (1975) before achieving stardom, writing the role of and portraying boxer Robert "Rocky" Balboa in the Rocky franchise (1976–present). For Rocky (1976) he was nominated for two Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor. He went on to reprise the role in Creed (2015) and Creed II (2018), the former of which earned him a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor as well as a Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture win. 
Stallone also portrayed John Rambo in First Blood (1982), a role he would play across five Rambo films (1982–2019) which he also co-wrote. He went on to become, from the mid-1980s to the late 1990s, one of Hollywood's highest-paid actors, acting in films such as Rhinestone (1984), Cobra (1986), Over the Top (1987), Tango and Cash (1989), Oscar (1991), Cliffhanger, Demolition Man (both 1993), The Specialist (1994), and Cop Land (1997). He later acted in The Expendables film franchise (2010–2014) and the Escape Plan film series (2013–2019). He portrayed Stakar Ogord in the Marvel Cinematic Universe films Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017) and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 (2023).
In television, he has starred in the Paramount+ crime series Tulsa King (2022–present) and the reality series The Family Stallone (2023–2024), both of which he also served as an executive producer. Stallone is also a noted art collector and painter, and has written books on fitness.

Early life
Sylvester Gardenzio Stallone was born in Hell's Kitchen in New York City on July 6, 1946, the elder son of celebrity astrologer and women's professional wrestling promoter Jacqueline "Jackie" Stallone (née Labofish; 1921–2020) and hairdresser Francesco "Frank" Stallone Sr. (1919–2011), who opened up and ran a group of hair salons in Maryland and was an avid polo player. His mother was an American from Washington, D.C., with Breton French and Ukrainian Jewish ancestry, while his father was an Italian immigrant from Gioia del Colle who moved to the U.S. in the 1930s. His younger brother is actor and musician Frank Stallone. grok_lead: Sylvester Gardenzio Stallone (born July 6, 1946 (age 79)) is an American actor, screenwriter, director, and producer recognized for his portrayals of resilient, working-class protagonists in action films. Best known for creating and starring as the underdog boxer Rocky Balboa in the Rocky series starting with the 1976 film Rocky, which he also wrote, and as the troubled Vietnam War veteran John Rambo in the Rambo franchise beginning with First Blood (1982), Stallone's characters embodied themes of personal perseverance and physical determination that resonated widely during the late 20th century. The Rocky film earned critical acclaim and commercial success, receiving ten Academy Award nominations, including for Best Picture (which it won), Best Director, Best Actor for Stallone, and Best Original Screenplay for his script, marking a breakthrough that propelled him to stardom after years of minor roles and financial struggles. The Rambo series, which he co-wrote and directed in later installments, further solidified his status in the action genre, grossing hundreds of millions at the box office and influencing depictions of military heroism in popular culture. Over a career spanning five decades, Stallone has achieved the rare feat of starring in films that opened at number one across multiple decades, including The Expendables (2010), while continuing to direct and produce projects that emphasize raw physicality and narrative grit.
